messages.author: 75db403eb2b8ba68
messages.subject: how to plot e.g. smooth y~x line inside scatterplots
parts:
I would like to use the boxplot area to show the relationhip between two numeric values. That would be instead of making two graphs: p1: boxplots for factor on y values _and_  p2 scatterplot for x values on y values

I would like to use geom_boxplot(fill=aes(x=x,y=y)+geom_smooth) - or something like that (maybe stat_smooth) - is this possible? - and is it clear what i'm trying to say :-)

example data:
x <- rnorm(100)
y <- rnorm(100)
faktor <- rep(c("this","that","bat","man"),25)
play <- data.frame(cbind(x,y,faktor))
play$x <- as.numeric(as.character(play$x))
play$y <- as.numeric(as.character(play$y))

ggplot(play,aes(x=faktor,y=y))+geom_boxplot() #this is where i woul like to use fill=smooth or similar

In that case, you explained it well the first time.

Unfortunately, I cannot offer any suggestions on this. For example,
the axes do not match, and I'm not sure how to combine these different
features.

I wonder if what you are trying to convey can be represented in a more
conventional manner.

It seems you want to show a trend, the spread of the raw data, and you
want this by group.

So, for example, you could facet the data by group, show the trend, a
confidence band, as well as the raw data. Would this convey the
features you would like to show?

Sorry I couldn't be more helpful.

As Juliet suggested you can get something similar to that using
facets, using the dataframe
you presented above you could do this:

ggplot(play, aes(x,y)) + geom_boxplot() + geom_smooth(se=FALSE) +
facet_grid(. ~ faktor)

HTH

david

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: how to plot e.g. smooth y~x line inside scatterplots
parts:
I guess it should be possible to create a new geom for this, although
I'm not quite convinced how well it represents the data (but then
again, I don't fully understand regular boxplots...)

A starting point would be to create a grob like this,


library(grid)
#' bloated box plot
#'
#' @aliases bboxGrob grid.bbox
#' @title bboxGrob
#' @param x coordinates
#' @param y coordinates
#' @return a grob
#' @seealso \code{grid.segments}, \code{grid.points}
#' @examples
#' r <-
#' gboxplot()
#' pushViewport(viewport())
#' grid.draw(r)


library(grid)
gboxplot <- function( x =seq(0, 1, len=100), y = rnorm(100, 0.6, 0.02),
ymin=0.2, lower=0.4, middle=0.7,
upper=0.8, ymax=0.9,
width=0.5) {
# smoothed data
b <- gList(
rectGrob(x = unit(0.5, "npc"), y = lower,
width = unit(width, "npc"), height = upper - lower,
just = "bottom", hjust = NULL, vjust = NULL,
default.units = "npc", name = NULL,
gp=gpar(fill="grey80"), vp = NULL),
segmentsGrob(x0=0.5-width/2, y0=middle, x1=0.5+width/2, y1=middle,
gp=gpar(col="grey50", lex=2)),
segmentsGrob(x0=rep(0.5, 2), x1=rep(0.5, 2),
y0=c(ymin, upper), y1=c(lower, ymax),
gp=gpar(lex=4, lineend="butt")))

s <- pointsGrob(x, y, vp=viewport(clip=TRUE, width=width))

g <- gTree(children=gList(b, s))
g
}

and once this is polished enough, an interface (mapping) could be made
via a new ggplot2 Geom. I'm not sure how one would specify the two
different statistics though.

Just a thought anyway,

Best,

baptiste
